passage:
Dear Manoj,
Thanks for Thursday. When you said I looked like a phone at two percent, I did my usual thing and made a joke about being "fine, just caffeinated." You didn't laugh, you just said, "Rest, Dhruv." I went home angry at how right you were. Then you turned up on Saturday with parathas and dragged me on that slow walk along the canal, and I finally admitted how tired I've been. I let you carry the plates. It felt strange to be looked after, but I slept properly for the first time in weeks. Next Saturday I'll bring the tea. Thank you for not letting me joke my way out of it 🙂
Dhruv

qa.q: What did Manoj bring on Saturday?
Why did Dhruv go home angry after Manoj's remark?
qa.a: Dhruv had joked about being "fine, just caffeinated" to hide the tiredness, and Manoj's plain "Rest, Dhruv" showed how right the concern was.

qa.q: Which small acts helped Dhruv begin to recover?
qa.a: The slow walk along the canal, the shared meal, letting Manoj carry the plates and finally sleeping properly.

qa.q: How might Manoj have felt when Dhruv answered with a joke?
qa.a: Probably worried, since Manoj did not laugh and repeated the advice to rest instead of letting it slide.

grounding: A friend notices exhaustion and says to rest; the person stops joking it away and accepts a walk and a shared meal as part of recovery.
